_note: Placements that are meant to look this way. tools\cli audit placement skips a problem whose kind matches and whose name or prefab matches the regex (docs/placement-audit.md). Give the reason a reviewer can check in a shot.

allow.why: The two police cars in the car-pool grid cell (#4352) stand on their wheels: place settle measured each mesh bottom 1 mm over GridTerrain; the audit's terrain check reads the vehicle pivot, which sits below the wheel tops.

The bag stands on the vault's own steel floor, 0.5 m above the terrain; the floor is part of the Roadmap_Bank_Vault mesh, so the trace down reads terrain (bank close-up c09, #925). It was hidden until the 'Map' in 'Roadmap_' stopped counting as a hung map.

The vault door is the prefab's own child (VaultDoor) on its hinge pivot, seated in the frame ring of VaultFront by design; in the _Open vault it stands on the same hinge beside the frame (tools/assets/bank-vault, #925). The town vault swings it open with the breach state.
The quarry axe lies flat on the ground by the logs (LoggingChain.layer angles 90).
The small money bag on the bank floor is meant to be small (#740).
The cash stack is the bag prefab's child, drawn inside the 0.4-scale bag the way the town bag is (#323 batch 0).
The cash stack is the bag prefab's child at 0.15 m, resting on the bag; the trace down reads terrain 0.17 m below the stack, not the bag (#2133).
The annex twin of the bank bell box hangs 1.5 m up beside the twin vault door: the annex has no wall for it, and the alarm mount test only needs the box above its door (#323 batch 0).
The teller stands inside the bank on its floor (y 0.2) behind the vanilla post-office counter; the terrain probe misses the building floor (#931).

Vanilla has no cabbage-head mesh, only the whole-plant CabbageCrop_01 (0.84 x 0.91 m at scale 1). Cabbage.et scales it to 0.5, so the plant measures 0.46 m, inside the cabbage 0.15-0.6 m range. A larger scale would put a 0.9 m plant on a stall table.
A market tarp is stretched between four poles 2.4 to 2.7 m up over its stall; nothing stands under it but the stall and its trader (market-canopies).
Flag_1_2 is a plain 1 x 2 m red cloth with a white hem; scaled 2x it is a 2 x 4 m tarp, the largest flat cloth in the base game (market-canopies).
The door hood and the bulkhead light are fixed to the vault front: their backs stand in the concrete face, as wall-mounted fittings do (polish-vault-market).

The market parasol stands at the back of the registry counter and its canopy reaches over the counter top on purpose: the clerk and the counter are under cover (arrival-desk look, town-arrival-desk). The pole stands clear of the counter; only the canopy box overlaps it.

The b16 bench stands on a pavement edge that falls 9 cm under its 1.6 m seat; it is seated on the highest of five probed points (street-life.mjs benchGround), so the low side shows a 1.4 cm gap at one foot.

Open hillside on Coalman's Brow: the ground falls 2 to 21 cm under each footprint (west to east), so the furnace (6 cm), the desk (2.8 cm), the pick pile (3.2 cm) and the work lamp (1.3 cm) bury their uphill side in the slope the way any prop on a bank does. Rows rest on the probed terrain (tools/town/terrain/coalmans-brow-mine.json), as on the Black Lake shore.
The spoil heaps beside the mine mouth are the vanilla GravelPile_01_base (8.28 m across), the same prop the mine-entrance and coal-pile kits use; a mine spoil heap is meant to be that large.

Open ground on the Black Lake shore: the slope falls 5 to 18 cm under each prop's footprint, so a bench (9.6 cm), the fishing spot (2.5 cm) and the lantern (1.2 cm) bury their uphill side in the hillside the way any prop on a bank does. Rows rest on the probed terrain (tools/town/terrain/blacklake-shore.json); a terrain-mount row takes no height offset.

The two doorstep benches stand on a sloping pavement whose height varies 6 to 10 cm under each 1.6 m seat; each is seated on the highest probed point of the paving (terrain.mjs SURFACE_HIT), so the low foot shows a gap of 1.4 to 1.6 cm.

A wheat or stubble patch is 3 m of alpha cards whose feet sit 4 cm under the pivot so no card edge shows; the field follows rolling ground, and the ground varies up to 15 cm across 3 m, so one side sinks into the earth as grass does (#3290).

LF_TownBoard has no static mesh: LF_SignComponent builds the cork panel at runtime and the card actions sit on that panel (0.12 m spheres at 1.5-1.8 m), so the audit reads the board as a point with no mesh near it. The panel renders (look place:montignac/depot, board close-up).

The timber lintel rests across the tops of the two upright log posts (MineEntrance_PostL/R, pitched 90, 3 m tall), 3 m above the terrain; the audit traces down to terrain only and does not read the pitched posts as support (contact sheet, #3857).

The two work lamps are wall lamps hung 2.8 m up on the -z wall of the plant shed (kit rows verb against wall, wall -z); a grid bay holds the kit without the shed shell, so the trace down reads open terrain (contact sheet, #3857). town fit seats them on the host wall.

The till rests on the host counter (CounterShop_01, flat top 1.039 m, island height 16.486): a row of probe radios at the same height read a contact gap of 0 cm over the whole of that top (2026-11-21, #3888 baseline cleanup), while the 3x3 contact trace reads a support 7 to 11 cm higher only under this till, moving with its x and not with its z. The same till prefab on the miner counter beside it measures clean. A measurement artefact of the host furniture, not a sunk till.
The plate is the vanilla full-size door number plate shipped at scale 0.5 on purpose: about 45 x 22 cm beside a house door (PLATE_SCALE and PLATE_BOX in tools/town/residenthomes.mjs).

Vanilla Everon road-works cones baked into the base map (roadside works on the island's roads, outside the fitted town streets); no layer row or script owns them and none can remove them. The sweep reads the whole island, so they appear as strays.
Furniture baked into the vanilla prefab's own children (boat sheds on the shore, a farm shed, a depot warehouse). No pack row or kit places it and a sub-layer cannot hide a prefab child (#3882).
A floodlight bolted to the site cabin roof edge: its bracket overlaps the cabin by design (it rests on the cabin top, contact 0).

A low scrap heap (1 m) 8 m wide in the dealer yard, wedged between the compound wall and a base-map tin-wall gate that is not used as a door; moving it 1 m either way clipped the wall or the gate more (tried 2026-11-21).
A wreck lying among the base-map junk at the dump edge; it touches a vanilla metal bin and moving it 1-3 m along the fence only swapped which clutter it touches (tried 2026-11-21).

The last scrap heap of the dump (7 m wide) sits between base-map tyre piles on one side and a birch and the blue container on the other; every shift of 0.7-2 m along the row only swapped which of them it touches (3 tries, 2026-11-21). A low heap among the dump clutter reads as intended.

The last scrap heap of the dump (7 m wide) sits between base-map tyre piles on one side and a birch and the blue container on the other; every shift of 0.7-2 m along the row only swapped which of them it touches (3 tries, 2026-11-21). A low heap among the dump clutter reads as intended.

A drop zone, not a prop: the entity is a mesh-less volume (7 m radius, 3 m high context; LF_GranaryUnloadAction half extents 5 x 3 x 7) that offers 'unload' to a hauler standing anywhere in the yard with the load, so there is no mesh to be near.

The display van parks at the foot of a base-map doorstep on the car lot's hillside (3 m of fall across its 5 m box); the stairs touch 2 of 9 rays by 13 cm at the wheel arch. Moving it with the kit put it into the workshop wall (tried 2026-11-21), so it stays against the steps.

The car parks under an apple tree (t_malus_domestica_2s) beside the b12 yard; the audit box is the whole tree with its crown. The slope here is steep and fenced: the island probe (town parked-cars --probe, 15 lines at 4 heights) refused all 13 other spots (net fence, 1.5 to 3 m of fall, a container, Eden walls), so the old spot stays (2026-11-22).

LF_BankVault_RoomDoor is a mesh-less root: its one mesh is the VaultDoor child leaf (1.27 m right of the root, hinged in the vault-room doorway), which the audit does not read as a mesh. The action context (radius 1.5 m at the front's centre, 0.45 m out) overlaps the leaf; the same prefab opens in the grid bank proof (#2384).

EL_JailDoor stands where the villa's own barred cell leaf (Door_PrisonCell_E_A_Left_INT_ST_B, a child of the DoorSet) hangs; the audit reads that leaf as a door. The kit's boxed clear (Fit_saint_philippe_jail_clear_box1) hides the vanilla leaf at runtime (server log 'hid 1 vanilla props in the box'), so only the placed door remains (island-jail-breach-proof).

The two wing leaves of the jail gate are fixed and locked (LF_LockComponent, no breach target, no open action), overlapping by 0.5 m on purpose so the 2.7 m corridor mouth has no gap; neither swings, so each reads the other as a door in its swing (gate close-up in the PR).

A market umbrella over the street end of the stall: its bounds are the 2.4 m canopy, so the stall under it overlaps that box and the canopy reaches past the kerb. Only the pole stands on the pavement, clear of the stall (look place:saint-philippe/market, first-two-hours review A20).

A market umbrella over the street end of the stall: its bounds are the 2.4 m canopy, so the stall under it overlaps that box and the canopy reaches past the kerb. Only the pole stands on the pavement, clear of the stall (look place:saint-philippe/market, first-two-hours review A20).

A market umbrella over the street end of the stall: its bounds are the 2.4 m canopy, so the stall under it overlaps that box and the canopy reaches past the kerb. Only the pole stands on the pavement, clear of the stall (look place:saint-philippe/market, first-two-hours review A20).
The stall stands under the market umbrella (Fit_saint_philippe_market_market_awning): the overlap is the canopy box over the stall end, not a solid touch (first-two-hours review A20).
The room roll-up of the same stall-under-umbrella overlap on the b01 pavement (first-two-hours review A20).

The town clothing store's till action sits on the Village_ClothingStore building itself, so the rule reads the whole shop as one till box and every action prop inside it as 0 m from it. The counter's price list and the mannequin are 3 m and 4 m from the real till point (the clerk counter at the door end); the island splits the till into its own LF_ClothesTill prefab and has no such box.

A bird flock (SCR_Bird) is a flock the engine moves: it spawns at its row (y equals the terrain here, 0 m over the ground) and the probe finds the flock entity wherever it has wandered, so the audit's position match fails. Rows stand on the cobbles beside the chess table (#4479).
